title: Sprint lift and reshuffle: company compact and all-hands playbook
body:
Purpose:
This compact is a short, tactical reference for the upcoming 6-week "sprint lift" where we (1) rebaseline near-term company priorities, (2) reshuffle deliverable ownership to reduce cross-team dependencies, and (3) align the all-hands and exec update narrative. The goal is to produce an updated set of company OKRs and a one-page rollout plan that engineering, product, and GTM can act on immediately.

Context / why now:
- Q1 usage patterns show uneven host/dedicated adoption; cost-per-unit variance higher than forecast (see PLAT-1182).
- Several mid-quarter infra risks require a concentrated focus window to avoid downstream slippage into Dedicated commitments.
- We need a simpler story for customers and sales ahead of the regional partner push in EMEA.

Timebox and cadence:
- Week 0 (Feb 10–16): intake + stakeholder interviews; capture risks and must-dos.
- Week 1 (Feb 17–23): draft OKR slate + prioritization matrix; engineering intake for feasibility.
- Week 2 (Feb 24–Mar 2): finalize OKRs; publish townline + run-of-show for all-hands.
- Week 3 (Mar 3–9): execute comms + owner-level signoffs; begin canary tasks.

Proposed company-level OKR draft (for review):
Objective A: Reduce inference cost variance and improve predictability for hosted/Dedicated customers.
- KR A1: Reduce per-request token cost variance (95th / median) by 30% for hosted API.
- KR A2: Cut tail latency incidents (>500ms above SLO) by 50% across top-10 enterprise customers.
- KR A3: Ship two routing+quantization playbooks and measure 10% effective cost reduction on 3 representative workloads.

Objective B: Make the Redwood runtime the default low-latency path for new model onboards.
- KR B1: Decrease median model onboard time from model-accepted to serving-ready to <= 7 days.
- KR B2: Publish performance profiles for 12 open models and integrate into Console recommendations.
- KR B3: Achieve 90% automated compatibility for model variants in smart-routing tests.

Objective C: Strengthen enterprise readiness and private deployment adoption.
- KR C1: Complete VPC installer reference for two major cloud providers + on-prem checklist.
- KR C2: Sign 3 pilot customers for Private deployment with SLA commitments.
- KR C3: Add audit-log export to the Console and demonstrate in one compliance review.

Prioritization & reshuffle matrix (summary):
- Tier 1 (Must ship this quarter): tail-latency triage + routing fallback; VPC installer beta; Console profiling for top 6 models. Owners: SRE, Platform, Console teams.
- Tier 2 (Accelerate if capacity): quantization playbook + optimize tooling; Dedicated autoscale policy tuning. Owners: Applied-ML, Optimize team.
- Tier 3 (Backlog / defer if necessary): experimental reranking infra; cross-region snapshots.

All-hands run-of-show (compact):
- 00:00–00:05 (MC: Priya): Welcome, readouts of the sprint purpose.
- 00:05–00:12 (CEO: Jordan Lee): Exec framing — why predictability and cost matter for our product-market fit.
- 00:12–00:25 (Product: Marco): OKR slate walk-through + quick Q&A (live upvote).
- 00:25–00:35 (Engineering: Samantha): Key technical bets and timeline for Tier 1 deliverables.
- 00:35–00:40 (SRE: Daniel): Risk heatmap and mitigation commitments.
- 00:40–00:50 (GTM: Aisha): Customer-facing narrative, partner readiness, and asks (case studies).
- 00:50–01:00 (MC): Live pulse (3 breakouts: infra blockers, rollout playbooks, customer comms).

Exec update talking points (one-pagers for each exec):
- High-level thesis: shift from model variety to serving certainty; measurable lever is cost/latency per use-case.
- What we will measure this cycle: variance, SLO breaches, model onboard time, enterprise acceptance rate.
- Ask of execs: commit to owner-level decisions within 48 hours on any cross-team dependency flagged during intake.

Comms plan (internal + external):
- Internal: publish townline + OKRs (Confluence) immediately after Week 2 finalization; weekly short standups for owners. Slack channel: #sprint-lift-2025.
- External: customer note for top 15 accounts with expected impact; partner briefing for EMEA integrators.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Tier 1 depends on a vendor kernel update; Mitigation: fall back to a validated quantized path and flag tradeoffs in Console.
- Risk: Too many owners without single decision-maker; Mitigation: assign a single R (responder) per Tier 1 deliverable with escalation path to COO.
- Risk: Comms noise confuses customers about model compatibility; Mitigation: coordinated FAQ + short video from Solutions Eng.

Decision log (to capture during the sprint):
- Feb 12: Preliminary decision to prioritize routing fallback over global autoscale modification (pending SRE feasibility).
- Feb 18: Tentative owner assignment for VPC installer -> Platform eng (Marco Reyes).

Open questions for exec forum:
- What is the appetite for temporarily reassigning 1–2 FTEs from growth into Platform for 6 weeks?
- Acceptable threshold for delaying Tier 2 items if Tier 1 shows slippage?

Next steps (this doc owner):
- Feb 18: Publish first-pass OKR doc and send calendar invite for cross-team intake (Aisha).
- Feb 20–21: 30-minute interviews with key stake-holders (SRE, Platform, Applied-ML, Console, GTM).
- Feb 24: Release townline and all-hands runbook for rehearsal (Priya to coordinate).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally compact — we want rapid iteration. Please add comments inline on Confluence: confluence:COMPANY-STRAT-2025-02 and flag any blockers with slack:@channel.
- If you have immediate objections to any KR targets, call out tradeoffs in-line in this draft.

Document history:
- v0-1 created Feb 10 by Aisha Patil.
- edits Feb 12 (incorporated SRE risk notes).
- Feb 18: updated owners and timeline after intake session.
